---
title: "Methods & Math"
subtitle: "Eikonal body-wave tomography"
---

Code lives in [AlaskaTomography](https://github.com/ajm-glitch/AlaskaTomography). The solver is [EikoHypoTomo](https://github.com/biondiettore/EikoHypoTomo) [@biondi2023], included as a submodule.

## Forward problem

First-arrival travel times $T$ from each source satisfy the Eikonal equation through the velocity model $v$:

$$
\lvert \nabla T(\mathbf{x}) \rvert = \frac{1}{v(\mathbf{x})}
$$

Travel times are computed for P and S to every DAS channel and broadband station, for each of the 400 catalog events.

**Code:** [`checkerboard_3D/forward_modeling.ipynb`](https://github.com/ajm-glitch/AlaskaTomography/blob/main/checkerboard_3D/forward_modeling.ipynb)

## Objective function

We minimize the misfit between observed and predicted travel times:

$$
\phi(\mathbf{v}) = \tfrac{1}{2}\,\big\lVert \mathbf{f}(\mathbf{v}) - \boldsymbol{\tau}_{obs} \big\rVert_2^2
$$

where $\boldsymbol{\tau}_{obs}$ are the observed travel times, $\mathbf{f}$ is the Eikonal operator, $\mathbf{v}$ is the velocity vector, and $\lambda$ weights the body-wave travel-time errors. The model is updated with BFGS (60 iterations in the June runs).

**Code:** the inversion is run from the [`Makefile`](https://github.com/ajm-glitch/AlaskaTomography/blob/main/Makefile):

```makefile
EikoDD_AKTest_20km_both: $(catalog) $(vel_model) | $(synthetic_data_dir)
	$(CONDA_RUN) python -u $(EIKO_MAIN) $@_TOMO 60 $(vel_model) \
	  --LocFile $(catalog) \
	  --Traveltimes $(synthetic_data_dir) \
	  --sigma_smoo 2.5 -par 2 --Ginsu 0 --saveResult 1 1 1 1
```

## Checkerboard tests

The synthetic model multiplies the starting model by a 3D cosine pattern with half-wavelength $L$ (the "checker size") and amplitude $a$ (5%):

$$
\delta v(x, y, z) = a\, v_0(x, y, z)\, \cos\!\left(\frac{\pi x}{L}\right) \cos\!\left(\frac{\pi y}{L}\right) \cos\!\left(\frac{\pi z}{L}\right)
$$

```python
sineY = np.cos(np.pi / size_check * yAxis)[:, None, None]
sineX = np.cos(np.pi / size_check * xAxis)[None, :, None]
sineZ = np.cos(np.pi / size_check * zAxis)[None, None, :]
checkerboardVp = sineX * sineY * sineZ * scale_anomaly * VpInit
```

Synthetic travel times through this model are inverted from the unperturbed starting model, and the recovered pattern is compared with the true one ([Results](../results/index.qmd)).

**Code:** [`checkerboard_3D/checkerboard_setup.ipynb`](https://github.com/ajm-glitch/AlaskaTomography/blob/main/checkerboard_3D/checkerboard_setup.ipynb), [`checkerboard_3D/evaluate_checkerboard_results.ipynb`](https://github.com/ajm-glitch/AlaskaTomography/blob/main/checkerboard_3D/evaluate_checkerboard_results.ipynb)

## Planned: covariance weighting

Separate DAS and broadband data covariances, so the dense, correlated DAS channels don't overwhelm the broadband data:

$$
\phi(\mathbf{v}) = \tfrac{1}{2}\,\mathbf{r}^{\mathsf T}\,\mathbf{C}_d^{-1}\,\mathbf{r},
\qquad \mathbf{r} = \mathbf{f}(\mathbf{v}) - \boldsymbol{\tau}_{obs},
\qquad \mathbf{C}_d = \begin{bmatrix} \mathbf{C}_{DAS} & \mathbf{0} \\ \mathbf{0} & \mathbf{C}_{BB} \end{bmatrix}
$$

DAS covariance terms: spatial correlation, pick noise, and model uncertainty.

## Planned: alternating relocation

1. Hold the velocity model fixed and relocate every event, using the picks and covariance weights.
2. Hold the new locations fixed and update the velocity model.
3. Repeat until the misfit stops improving.
